primary_source.paper: Wei et al. 2022, "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models"

trace_source: tasks/parity_coinflip/published_trace.txt -- Wei et al. 2022 Fig. 3 / Appendix G 8-shot CoT prompt for Coin Flip, corroborated verbatim via third-party reproductions (ArmelRandy/tree-of-problems, HKUNLP/HumanPrompt, xlang-ai/batch-prompting, others; see file header). No trace exists for the raw-parity variant (Anil et al. 2022's scratchpad figure is image-only in the PDF; no text-extractable exemplar found anywhere) -- every metric below describes the coin-flip framing only.
format_description: A single free-form narrative sentence that counts total flip events across the whole chain and states the parity of that count in words (e.g. "flipped 1 time, which is an odd number"), then derives heads/tails from the start state -- NOT a per-person or per-step scratchpad line; the published CoT never itemizes each person's flip decision individually.
theory_citation: Chiang & Cholak 2022, "Overcoming a Theoretical Limitation of Self-Attention" (ACL 2022, arXiv:2202.12172; code github.com/ndnlp/parity) construct an explicit constant-depth transformer that computes PARITY exactly, so parity/coin-flip is NOT provably serial for transformers despite being canonically 'inherently sequential' for RNNs/finite automata. Bhattamishra et al. 2020 (EMNLP, "On the Ability of Self-Attention Networks to Recognize Counter Languages") independently show self-attention can recognize parity-adjacent counter languages under suitable positional encodings.

published_data.metric: PaLM 540B accuracy, standard vs chain-of-thought prompting, Coin Flip
published_data.values: standard prompting 98.1%; CoT prompting 100.0% (per-text extraction via ar5iv render, flagged for a check against the original PDF/figure -- the paper's headline coin-flip result concerns OOD length generalization, i.e. training exemplars show 2 flips and test chains are longer, where standard prompting's advantage over CoT is expected to be much smaller than these in-domain-looking numbers suggest; treat this row as needing verification of which condition -- in-domain vs OOD -- it reports)

published_data.paper: Anil et al. 2022, "Exploring Length Generalization in Large Language Models" (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2207.04901)
published_data.metric: Length generalization of raw parity under scratchpad/CoT prompting vs finetuning alone
published_data.models: not publicly specified which base checkpoints (Google-internal)
published_data.values: qualitative only: scratchpad prompting dramatically improves length generalization on parity relative to finetuning-only or prompting-only baselines, but every technique/combination shows distinct failure modes as length grows; no single numeric table extracted (paper presents this primarily as generalization curves, and no trace/figure text was recoverable for exact values)

published_data.metric: Theoretical + small-scale empirical characterization of which counter languages self-attention networks recognize
published_data.models: small trained Transformer encoders (toy study, not a benchmarked frontier LLM)
published_data.values: no single headline accuracy number applies; framing/theory citation only

published_data.metric: Existence of a constant-depth transformer construction computing PARITY exactly
published_data.models: hand-constructed small Transformer, not a pretrained LLM
published_data.values: 100% by construction (proof, not an empirical benchmark run)

notes: Central finding of this desk pass: the WIDELY-CITED published coin-flip CoT format is a global counting shortcut ('flipped N times, N is odd/even'), not a per-person state-tracking scratchpad -- this matches the explicit observation in the 'Self-Harmonized Chain of Thought' paper that human-written Few-shot-CoT prompts for this task 'employ a shortcut solution by counting overall flips' rather than tracking state step by step, in contrast to some automatically-generated CoTs that do track state explicitly. Because of this, step_delimitable, state_at_fixed_position, error_diagnostic, and interp_tractable are all FALSE for the format as published, even though the underlying task (heads/tails toggling under an XOR chain) has a maximally step-local, high-redundancy structure (state_k = state_{k-1} XOR flip_k) that WOULD support a rigid, highly interpretable per-step scratchpad if we chose to write one -- that is a design choice for our own task.py, not something the literature already provides. tokens_per_step/steps_in_trace/state_atomic_tokens/knob.tokens_flat_across_knob are null because the published trace has no discrete step boundaries to divide by, and only one exemplar (depth=2 flip-events) was locatable, so nothing about flatness-across-depth could be measured. 50% guessing floor still applies to the underlying binary answer regardless of prompting format. No usable existing generator/dataset/wrapper was found for either the coin-flip or raw-parity framing (see SOURCING.md from the phase-1 pass); task.py, if and when written, must be built from scratch. Tokenizers used: unsloth/gemma-2-2b (mirror; google/gemma-2-2b is gated and inaccessible without an HF token in this environment), NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B (mirror; meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B is likewise gated), Qwen/Qwen2-7B (ungated, fetched directly). Per amendment 2's own instruction to never hand-estimate, all token counts above are real tokenizer.json encodes, not estimates.
